questions.q: Which paint brand is the manufacturer of the 'Liquid Tile' product line?
questions.n: Davies is the specific manufacturer that markets the Liquid Tile line of specialized coatings.

questions.q: What is the recommended thinner for Acrylic Latex paint?
questions.n: Acrylic latex is a water-borne emulsion, making water the primary and recommended thinning agent.

questions.q: Among the following, which is considered the most expensive material for bathtubs?
questions.n: Cast iron with porcelain enamel is extremely heavy, durable, and carries the highest material and installation cost.

questions.q: What is the primary thinner for Oil-based or Enamel paints?
questions.n: These petroleum distillates are designed to dissolve the resins in oil-based and enamel coatings.

questions.q: Which glass type is used for car windshields and skylights due to its safety properties?
questions.n: Laminated glass uses an interlayer that holds shards in place upon impact, preventing them from falling or flying.

questions.q: Which glass type is recommended for stairs or glass floors for structural safety?
questions.n: This combination provides the high strength of tempering with the shard-retention of lamination for structural integrity.

questions.q: What type of glass should be used for T&B enclosures that need to withstand heat and impact?
questions.n: Tempered glass is heat-resistant and 4-5 times stronger than regular glass, breaking into safe granules if hit.

questions.q: Identify a local manufacturer of Portland Cement in the Philippines.
questions.n: These are the dominant players in the Philippine cement industry.

questions.q: Identify a local manufacturer of Reinforcing Steel Bars (RSB).
questions.n: SteelAsia is the Philippines' largest manufacturer of reinforcing steel bars.

questions.q: What is the common brand for intercom systems in the Philippines?
questions.n: Aiphone is a leading global brand widely used for building and residential intercoms in the Philippines.

questions.q: Which brand is known for fans and appliances but NOT for manufacturing air conditioning units?
questions.n: Asahi is famous for electric fans and small appliances but does not produce AC units.

questions.q: Which material is best used for 'Soffit' or 'Eaves' finishes to resist moisture and rot?
questions.n: These materials are inorganic and resistant to moisture, making them ideal for exposed outdoor finishes.

questions.q: What is 'MDF' in wood materials?
questions.n: MDF is an engineered wood product made by breaking down wood residuals into wood fibers and combining them with wax and resin.

questions.q: What is 'HDF'?
questions.n: HDF is a denser, stronger version of MDF, often used for flooring and cabinets.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between MDF and Marine Plywood?
o: MDF is made of wood layers while Marine Plywood is made of fibers.
MDF is stronger than Marine Plywood.
Marine plywood is water-resistant (using Type I glue); MDF swells when exposed to moisture.
There is no functional difference in moisture environments.
questions.n: The key distinction is the binder and structure; marine plywood survives water while MDF does not.

questions.q: Which material is used as a filler for expansion joints in concrete pavements?
questions.n: These asphalt-based materials are flexible and can compress/expand as the concrete moves.

questions.q: What is the coverage rate of 1 gallon of paint for a single coat on a smooth surface?
questions.n: This is the industry standard estimate for coverage on a non-porous, smooth substrate.

questions.q: Which material is used for 'Spandrel' in building facades?
o: Aluminum or Glass panels covering the floor slabs
questions.n: Spandrel panels are the opaque sections of a curtain wall that hide the mechanical systems and slab edges.

questions.q: What is the standard gap for a construction joint?
o: No gap is needed; they are butt-jointed.
Typically 6mm to 10mm depending on the sealant type
questions.n: This gap provides sufficient space for the joint sealant to expand and contract without failing.

questions.q: Which roofing material is known for being lightweight and corrosion-resistant?
questions.n: Galvalume (Aluminum-Zinc alloy) offers superior corrosion resistance compared to standard galvanizing.

questions.q: Which joint is made by cutting a slot into the end of one board and a corresponding tab on the other?
questions.n: The mortise is the slot (hole) and the tenon is the tab (projection) that fits into it.

questions.q: What is a 'Dado' joint?
o: A groove cut across the grain of a board to receive the end of another board
A hole drilled for a screw
questions.n: Dados are horizontal grooves commonly used for shelving in bookcases.

questions.q: What is a 'Rabbet' joint?
o: A hole cut in the center of a board
A 90-degree corner joint with no grooves
A recess or groove cut into the edge or end of a board
questions.n: Rabbets are L-shaped grooves cut into the edge of a workpiece.

questions.q: Which joint uses a small, oval-shaped wood piece to reinforce the connection?
questions.n: The 'biscuit' is a compressed wood oval that swells when glued, creating a strong bond.

questions.q: What is a 'Box Joint'?
o: A joint used only for round containers
A finger-like interlocking joint used for the corners of boxes
A joint shaped like a dove's tail
A joint reinforced with steel plates
questions.n: Also called a finger joint, it consists of rectangular 'fingers' that intermesh.

questions.q: Which joinery is best for drawers to resist pulling forces?
questions.n: The trapezoidal shape of the pins physically prevents the joint from being pulled apart in one direction.

questions.q: What do you call a joint where two pieces are cut at 45 degrees?
questions.n: Commonly used for picture frames and door casings to hide end grain.

questions.q: What is a 'Pocket Joint'?
o: A joint reinforced with glue in small pockets
A joint using a pre-drilled angled hole to hide screws
A joint where one board slides into a pocket in another
A joint hidden inside a wall pocket
questions.n: Pocket hole joinery allows for fast, strong connections using specialized screws and jigs.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'Coped Joint'?
o: To join two pieces of wood end-to-end
To create a waterproof seal in joinery
Used in baseboards/molding where one piece is cut to the profile of the other to fit internal corners
To allow wood to expand and contract freely
questions.n: Coping prevents gaps that occur with miters when walls are not perfectly square.

questions.q: How is a door jamb measured for ordering?
o: By the diagonal of the door
Usually by the outside face of the jamb or the 'rough opening' of the wall
By the interior clear width only
By the height of the door leaf only
questions.n: The rough opening ensures the jamb assembly will fit within the structural frame.

questions.q: Which insulation material is made from molten rock or slag?
questions.n: Also known as mineral wool, it is manufactured by spinning molten volcanic rock.

questions.q: Which insulation is made from molten glass?
questions.n: Fiberglass insulation is composed of fine fibers of glass.

questions.q: What is 'EPS' in insulation?
questions.n: EPS is the common white foam used for packaging and low-cost insulation.

questions.q: What is 'XPS'?
o: Extruded Polystyrene (Usually blue or pink, more moisture resistant)
questions.n: XPS has a closed-cell structure making it denser and more water-resistant than EPS.

questions.q: Which insulation material is recommended for asthmatic users because it doesn't shed fibers?
questions.n: Polyester is made of long, continuous fibers that do not break off and become airborne.

questions.q: Which material provides both thermal insulation and high fire resistance?
questions.n: Because it is made of stone, it has a very high melting point and acts as a fire barrier.

questions.q: What is Polyurethane spray foam used for?
o: To increase the weight of the building
To serve as a finish floor material
Creating an airtight, high-R-value thermal barrier in roofs and walls
questions.n: It expands to fill gaps, providing both insulation and air sealing.

questions.q: Where is the 'Vapor Barrier' typically placed in a wall assembly?
o: In the middle of the insulation
On both sides of the insulation
On the cold side of the insulation
On the warm side of the insulation to prevent condensation
questions.n: This prevents warm, moist indoor air from reaching cold surfaces inside the wall.

questions.q: What is the 'R-value' in insulation?
o: The measure of a material's resistance to heat flow
questions.n: The higher the R-value, the better the material is at insulating.

questions.q: Which material is used for radiant barriers under a roof?
questions.n: The shiny surface reflects radiant heat away from the attic space.

questions.q: What is the standard 'Camber' for a 300cm (3m) concrete slab?
o: Approximately 6mm (rule of thumb is 2mm per meter)
questions.n: Camber is an intentional upward curve built into a beam or slab to compensate for future deflection.

questions.q: What structural element is designed to carry loads primarily in compression?
questions.n: Columns are vertical members meant to transmit axial compressive loads to the foundation.

questions.q: Which structural member prevents the twisting or sagging of purlins?
questions.n: Sagrods are thin rods used to align and support purlins against sagging along their weak axis.

questions.q: What is a 'King Post'?
o: The central vertical post in a roof truss
The largest column in a building
The post used to support a mailbox
questions.n: The king post extends from the apex down to the tie beam in a simple truss.

questions.q: What is a 'Lintel Beam'?
o: A beam placed over a door or window opening
A beam that supports the entire roof
A beam used to join two columns
A beam buried in the ground
questions.n: Lintels carry the load of the wall above an opening to the sides.

questions.q: What is 'Post-tensioning'?
o: Adding extra tension to a fence post
Stretching the steel tendons before the concrete is poured
Stretching the steel tendons after the concrete has cured
Using posts to hold up a tensile fabric roof
questions.n: Post-tensioning is done on-site after the concrete gains strength to allow for thinner slabs.

questions.q: What is 'Pre-tensioning'?
o: Stretching the steel tendons after the concrete is poured
Stretching the steel tendons before the concrete is poured
Tensioning the bolts in a steel connection
questions.n: Usually done in a factory setting, tendons are pulled tight and concrete is cast around them.

questions.q: In a slab, if the ratio of the long side to the short side is greater than 2, what type of slab is it?
questions.n: When one side is significantly longer, the load is assumed to travel primarily in one direction.

questions.q: What do you call a slab with ribs in both directions?
questions.n: The grid pattern creates a waffle-like appearance underneath.

questions.q: What is a 'Composite Slab'?
o: A slab mixed with plastic fibers
A slab that uses wood and stone
A slab made of two different types of concrete
A slab made of corrugated steel decking and concrete working together
questions.n: The metal deck acts as both formwork and permanent reinforcement.
